headline: Australian Unemployment Surges to 4.9%, Quashing Interest Rate Hike Expectations
summary: Australia's unemployment rate jumped to 4.9% in October from 4.7% in September, reaching its highest post-pandemic level. Major commercial banks stated the unexpected surge effectively rules out further central bank rate increases.
why: Labor market condition changes guide the Reserve Bank of Australia's rate decisions, directly impacting Australian sovereign bond yields, commercial mortgage rates, and the Australian dollar.

impacts.name: Australian Dollar
impacts.why: Rising unemployment reduced expectations for RBA rate hikes, pushing down local yield expectations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: The jump in October jobless figures led economists and money markets to price out further central bank monetary tightening.
